name: math_set_cardinality

phase_0.boundary_condition: The Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms with Choice (ZFC) providing the universe of discourse.

VINIT.justification: The initial object from which all sets are constructed via the power set and union axioms.

TANCH.chosen_element: The Class of All Sets V
TANCH.justification: The ultimate boundary containing every possible set cardinality within the hierarchy.

AFWD.justification: A directed mapping that establishes a lower bound on cardinality.

AREV.justification: A reverse mapping that collapses a larger set onto a smaller one to verify size constraints.

CLINK.justification: The sequential chaining of mappings to relate disparate sets through intermediate cardinalities.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-referential mapping that confirms a set is equinumerous with itself.

FSPLIT.justification: Splitting a set into a subset and its complement to test for specific properties like finiteness or countability.

FFUSE.justification: Reconstituting the original set from its partitioned subsets to verify the conservation of elements.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative state where a bijection is successfully established.

EVALF.justification: The negative state where no bijection exists, typically proven via diagonalization.

ENGAGR.justification: A state where a proposition is independent of the axioms, held as both potentially true and false.

IFIX.justification: The permanent fixation of a set's size into a specific transfinite cardinal number.

phase_3.void_description: The uninitialized state before the definition of any set or mapping.
phase_3.true_description: The existence of a bijective mapping between two sets.
phase_3.false_description: The absence of a bijective mapping, indicating a difference in cardinality.
phase_3.both_description: The undecidability of a cardinality relation within a specific axiomatic framework.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the empty set as the base for cardinality construction
Establish the identity of the set under investigation
Branch the set into a candidate subset and its complement for comparison
Attempt an injective mapping from the subset to a target cardinal
Confirm the mapping covers the target set elements
Attempt a surjective mapping back to the original set
Identify elements in the target set not reached by the mapping
Recombine the subset and complement to verify the total set size
Compose the mappings to form a candidate bijection
Evaluate the set against the Continuum Hypothesis to check for intermediate sizes
Permanently record the resulting cardinal value in the reference entry
Close the operation within the bounds of the ZFC universe

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The logical inference engine of ZFC set theory
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The formal language of first-order logic and set membership
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The cumulative hierarchy of sets (Von Neumann universe)
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The transfinite induction process determining the order of cardinal construction
phase_5.alfs_store: The CLINK L8 Organism catalog entry for math_set_cardinality

phase_6.cycle_cost: Logical processing cycles required for bijection verification
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A set with a fixed and recorded cardinal number
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The mapping process is a reversible transformation that preserves the information content of the set.
